reasoning: Recent polling in North Carolina’s 2026 U.S. Senate race consistently shows Democrat Roy Cooper leading Republican Michael Whatley by mid- to high-single digits, with one high-quality poll finding an 11-point advantage among likely voters, suggesting a current environment of roughly D+8–10 in the Senate contest despite the state’s slight R+1 structural tilt. There is no new, state-specific general-election presidential polling within the last 45 days in the retrieved results, so the best current quantified margin applies to the Senate race, where multiple reputable polls and news writeups agree Cooper is clearly ahead. Overall, the short-term polling picture points to a Democratic edge in the Senate race in a structurally Republican-leaning state.
